questions.scenarioContext: A financial services firm uses an encrypted web application. Its current network sensor records source and destination IP addresses and TCP ports, but the incident response team must distinguish approved application transactions from malicious requests inside established sessions.
questions.prompt: Which change would BEST provide the required visibility?

choices.A: Add a passive tap that records the same network-layer headers at higher speed
choices.B: Deploy application-aware inspection where authorized TLS traffic can be decrypted and examined
choices.C: Replace the access switches with devices that maintain larger MAC address tables
choices.D: Collect additional routing metrics from the edge routers

questions.explanation: Application-aware inspection at an authorized decryption point can evaluate requests within TLS sessions. A faster tap still sees only encrypted payloads and headers, while MAC tables and routing metrics provide link- or network-layer information rather than application transaction content.

questions.competency: IV.A — Network Architecture Fundamentals
questions.skill: Applying IPv6 security controls consistently with IPv4 controls
questions.performanceIndicator: Recognize and close a dual-stack network security coverage gap
questions.scenarioContext: A manufacturer enables IPv6 on a dual-stack production network. Firewall rules and monitoring signatures have been carefully tuned for IPv4, but no equivalent review has been performed for IPv6.
questions.prompt: What should the security architect do FIRST?

choices.A: Disable IPv4 so all traffic follows a single protocol stack
choices.B: Block all ICMPv6 messages at the perimeter
choices.C: Create equivalent IPv6 filtering and monitoring coverage and test both protocol paths
choices.D: Rely on network address translation to conceal all internal IPv6 addresses

questions.explanation: A dual-stack environment creates two usable network paths, so security policy, filtering, and monitoring must cover and test both. Disabling IPv4 may disrupt services, blocking all ICMPv6 interferes with essential IPv6 functions, and address translation is neither a substitute for controls nor generally required for IPv6.

questions.competency: IV.A — Network Architecture Fundamentals
questions.skill: Selecting an appropriate delivery model for one-to-many traffic
questions.performanceIndicator: Differentiate unicast, multicast, and broadcast communication requirements
questions.scenarioContext: A university must deliver the same live lecture stream to hundreds of authorized receivers across a managed campus network. The network team wants to minimize duplicate traffic across shared links without sending the stream to every host.
questions.prompt: Which transport approach BEST meets the requirement?

choices.A: A separate unicast stream for every receiver
choices.B: A subnet-wide broadcast stream
choices.C: A multicast stream with controlled group membership
choices.D: An anycast address assigned to every receiver

questions.explanation: Multicast efficiently distributes one stream to subscribed group members and avoids a separate copy for every receiver. Unicast duplicates traffic, broadcast reaches hosts that did not request the content, and anycast routes a client toward one of several service instances rather than distributing one stream to many receivers.

questions.competency: IV.A — Network Architecture Fundamentals
questions.skill: Evaluating security implications of encapsulated traffic
questions.performanceIndicator: Identify how multilayer tunneling can bypass intended inspection points
questions.scenarioContext: A research organization permits outbound HTTPS through a stateful firewall. Analysts discover that unmanaged hosts can encapsulate an unauthorized protocol inside allowed TLS connections, preventing the firewall from classifying the inner traffic.
questions.prompt: Which control would BEST address the risk while preserving approved web access?

choices.A: Allow outbound connections based only on destination port 443
choices.B: Increase the firewall session timeout for encrypted connections
choices.C: Apply authenticated application-aware egress controls at an authorized inspection point
choices.D: Replace all internal private addresses with publicly routable addresses

questions.explanation: Authenticated, application-aware egress inspection can distinguish approved web use from an unauthorized protocol hidden within TLS. Port-only rules cannot identify the inner protocol, longer timeouts do not improve classification, and public addressing does not solve encapsulation or inspection limitations.

questions.competency: IV.A — Network Architecture Fundamentals
questions.skill: Mapping network functions to OSI layers
questions.performanceIndicator: Identify the information available to controls operating at different layers
questions.prompt: Which TWO statements correctly describe network-layer visibility? Select 2 of the 5 options below.

choices.A: A Layer 2 switch normally forwards frames using MAC address information.
choices.B: A standard router selects paths primarily by inspecting HTTP request methods.
choices.C: A transport-layer control can use TCP or UDP port information when enforcing policy.
choices.D: An application proxy is limited to source and destination MAC addresses.
choices.E: An Ethernet broadcast is routed unchanged across every enterprise subnet by default.

questions.explanation: Layer 2 switches use MAC information, and transport-aware controls can evaluate TCP or UDP ports. Routers primarily make forwarding decisions from network-layer addressing, application proxies can inspect higher-layer content, and routers normally bound Ethernet broadcast domains rather than forwarding broadcasts everywhere.

questions.competency: IV.B — Segmentation, Wireless, and Modern Network Design
questions.skill: Designing segmentation for an Internet-facing service
questions.performanceIndicator: Place public services in a controlled network zone with restricted trust paths
questions.scenarioContext: A regional retailer is deploying an Internet-facing ordering server that must query an internal database. Administrators also need to manage the server from a protected workstation network.
questions.prompt: Which architecture provides the BEST defense in depth?

choices.A: Place the web server and database on the user LAN and filter only Internet traffic
choices.B: Place the web server in a DMZ, allow only required database flows, and use a separate managed administration path
choices.C: Place the database in the DMZ and allow the web server unrestricted access to the internal network
choices.D: Place both servers directly on the Internet and rely on host authentication

questions.explanation: A DMZ limits exposure of the public server, narrowly scoped database rules reduce lateral movement, and a separate managed path protects administration. The other designs collapse trust boundaries, expose sensitive systems, or rely too heavily on host controls alone.

questions.competency: IV.B — Segmentation, Wireless, and Modern Network Design
questions.skill: Selecting enterprise wireless authentication controls
questions.performanceIndicator: Choose wireless authentication that provides individual identity and strong mutual assurance
questions.scenarioContext: A consulting firm is replacing a shared wireless passphrase because former contractors may retain it. The firm wants per-user or per-device revocation and strong resistance to credential-capture access points.
questions.prompt: Which solution BEST satisfies these objectives?

choices.A: WPA3-Enterprise with certificate-based EAP authentication and validated server certificates
choices.B: WPA3-Personal using one complex passphrase rotated annually
choices.C: A hidden network name combined with MAC address filtering
choices.D: An open wireless network that requires users to accept a captive portal

questions.explanation: WPA3-Enterprise with certificate-based EAP supports individual credentials, targeted revocation, and mutual authentication when clients validate the authentication server. A shared passphrase lacks granular revocation, while hidden names, MAC filtering, and captive portals do not provide equivalent authentication assurance.

questions.competency: IV.B — Segmentation, Wireless, and Modern Network Design
questions.skill: Protecting a software-defined network control plane
questions.performanceIndicator: Prioritize controls for a centralized network control function
questions.scenarioContext: A logistics company adopts software-defined networking. A centralized controller programs forwarding behavior across many data-plane devices, increasing the impact of controller compromise.
questions.prompt: What is the MOST important security design consideration?

choices.A: Permit management access from every production subnet to simplify operations
choices.B: Protect controller access with strong authentication, restricted management paths, and resilient deployment
choices.C: Move all packet-forwarding decisions from switches to end-user devices
choices.D: Use a single shared administrator account to maintain policy consistency

questions.explanation: The controller is a high-impact control-plane component, so tightly restricted access, strong authentication, and resilience are essential. Broad management reachability and shared accounts increase compromise risk, while shifting forwarding decisions to endpoints defeats the intended architecture.

questions.competency: IV.B — Segmentation, Wireless, and Modern Network Design
questions.skill: Applying micro-segmentation to limit east-west movement
questions.performanceIndicator: Select workload-level policy enforcement for dynamic cloud systems
questions.scenarioContext: A media company runs hundreds of rapidly changing cloud workloads on the same private address space. Traditional subnet boundaries do not adequately restrict east-west communication between application tiers.
questions.prompt: Which approach BEST reduces lateral movement without depending solely on subnet placement?

choices.A: Assign policy to workload identities and permit only required service-to-service flows
choices.B: Increase the size of each subnet so workloads change addresses less often
choices.C: Route all internal traffic through a public content delivery network
choices.D: Allow unrestricted traffic between private addresses and inspect only north-south flows

questions.explanation: Identity-based micro-segmentation follows dynamic workloads and limits communication to explicitly required flows. Larger subnets and unrestricted private traffic expand lateral movement opportunities, while a content delivery network is intended primarily for content distribution and does not replace internal workload controls.

questions.competency: IV.B — Segmentation, Wireless, and Modern Network Design
questions.skill: Combining content delivery and origin protection controls
questions.performanceIndicator: Identify complementary controls for secure content delivery architecture
questions.scenarioContext: An online publisher uses a content delivery network for a public site. The origin server should accept content requests only through the delivery service, and administrative access must remain separate from the public delivery path.
questions.prompt: Which TWO controls BEST support the design? Select 2 of the 5 options below.

choices.A: Restrict origin ingress to authenticated or approved delivery-service paths.
choices.B: Expose the origin directly so clients can bypass a failed delivery node.
choices.C: Use a separate, strongly authenticated management path for the origin.
choices.D: Permit administrative access through the same anonymous public endpoint.
choices.E: Trust any request containing a client-supplied forwarding header.

questions.explanation: Restricting origin ingress prevents direct bypass of the delivery layer, while a separate authenticated management path isolates privileged access. Direct exposure weakens origin protection, anonymous administration collapses trust boundaries, and client-supplied headers are not reliable proof of an approved path.

questions.competency: IV.C — Securing Network Components
questions.skill: Choosing between detection and prevention controls
questions.performanceIndicator: Match an intrusion control's operating mode to availability and response requirements
questions.scenarioContext: A hospital wants to detect malicious traffic on a latency-sensitive clinical network. Blocking a legitimate session could disrupt care, and the organization has not yet tuned signatures against representative traffic.
questions.prompt: What is the BEST initial deployment approach?

choices.A: Deploy the system inline in blocking mode with every signature enabled
choices.B: Begin with passive detection, tune and validate alerts, then evaluate selective prevention
choices.C: Disable network monitoring because availability has priority
choices.D: Route clinical traffic through an unauthenticated public proxy

questions.explanation: Passive detection allows the hospital to establish accuracy and tune signatures without initially risking interruption of clinical traffic. Immediate broad blocking creates unacceptable false-positive risk, disabling monitoring sacrifices visibility, and a public proxy neither addresses the requirement nor protects the traffic.

questions.competency: IV.C — Securing Network Components
questions.skill: Using proxy controls to enforce outbound web policy
questions.performanceIndicator: Select a network component that mediates and records application requests
questions.scenarioContext: A government agency must enforce destination categories, authenticate employees, scan permitted web downloads, and retain centralized records of outbound browser requests.
questions.prompt: Which component BEST meets these requirements?

choices.A: A forward proxy with user authentication and content inspection
choices.B: A Layer 2 repeater on each office floor
choices.C: A load balancer in front of the agency's public website
choices.D: A passive fiber coupler with no policy engine

questions.explanation: A forward proxy can mediate employee web requests, associate them with identities, enforce category policy, scan content, and centralize logs. Repeaters and passive media components do not enforce application policy, while an inbound load balancer serves a different traffic direction and purpose.

questions.competency: IV.C — Securing Network Components
questions.skill: Hardening switch access against unauthorized devices
questions.performanceIndicator: Combine port admission and switching safeguards at the access layer
questions.scenarioContext: At a branch office, unused wall jacks remain connected. The security team also observes attempts to impersonate authorized device addresses and introduce unauthorized switching behavior.
questions.prompt: Which action would MOST directly reduce these access-layer risks?

choices.A: Disable unused ports and enforce authenticated network admission with appropriate switch protections
choices.B: Increase the dynamic routing protocol's convergence timer
choices.C: Publish the switch management interface through the guest wireless network
choices.D: Move the branch's public web server into the employee VLAN

questions.explanation: Disabling unused ports removes easy physical entry points, while authenticated admission and switch safeguards address impersonation and unauthorized access-layer behavior. Routing timers do not secure wall jacks, and exposing management or moving a public server into the employee segment increases risk.

questions.competency: IV.C — Securing Network Components
questions.skill: Designing secure load balancer health checks and administration
questions.performanceIndicator: Protect network service availability without creating privileged access paths
questions.scenarioContext: A software company uses load balancers to distribute customer requests across application servers. Security review finds that health checks use a privileged application account and the management interface is reachable from the public listener network.
questions.prompt: Which remediation is BEST?

choices.A: Use least-privileged health checks and isolate management on a restricted administrative network
choices.B: Disable health checks and send traffic to every server regardless of status
choices.C: Grant the health-check account database administrator privileges
choices.D: Expose each application server directly to eliminate the load balancer

questions.explanation: Least-privileged health checks limit credential impact, and an isolated management plane reduces exposure of administrative functions. Disabling checks harms availability, additional privilege worsens compromise impact, and direct server exposure removes useful protection without correcting the underlying design.

questions.competency: IV.C — Securing Network Components
questions.skill: Applying network access control to unmanaged endpoints
questions.performanceIndicator: Select complementary admission responses based on device identity and posture
questions.scenarioContext: A professional services firm permits employee laptops on its wired network. It must verify device identity and security posture before granting access, while giving noncompliant devices a limited path to approved remediation services.
questions.prompt: Which TWO capabilities BEST meet the requirement? Select 2 of the 5 options below.

choices.A: Authenticated network admission tied to device or user identity
choices.B: Unrestricted production access based only on possession of an Ethernet cable
choices.C: Dynamic placement of failed devices into a restricted remediation segment
choices.D: Permanent administrator privileges for every admitted endpoint
choices.E: Disabling endpoint posture assessment to reduce connection time

questions.explanation: Authenticated admission establishes identity, and dynamic restricted placement lets noncompliant devices reach only remediation resources. Cable possession is not sufficient assurance, administrator privileges are unrelated and dangerous, and disabling posture checks defeats a stated requirement.

questions.competency: IV.D — Secure Communication Channels
questions.skill: Selecting appropriate IPsec modes for site connectivity
questions.performanceIndicator: Choose a secure channel architecture that protects traffic between network gateways
questions.scenarioContext: A construction company needs persistent encrypted connectivity between two offices across an untrusted network. Internal hosts should not require individual tunnel configuration, and the original internal packets should be carried between security gateways.
questions.prompt: Which solution BEST satisfies the requirements?

choices.A: IPsec tunnel mode between the two gateways
choices.B: IPsec transport mode configured only between two individual workstations
choices.C: An unencrypted application proxy at one office
choices.D: A broadcast relay across the untrusted network

questions.explanation: IPsec tunnel mode between gateways encapsulates and protects the original packets for site-to-site connectivity without configuring every internal host. Host-only transport mode does not meet the network-wide requirement, and neither an unencrypted proxy nor a broadcast relay provides the required protected channel.

questions.competency: IV.D — Secure Communication Channels
questions.skill: Protecting VoIP signaling and media across trust boundaries
questions.performanceIndicator: Apply layered safeguards to real-time voice communications
questions.scenarioContext: A legal services organization is deploying Internet-connected voice communications. It must protect call setup and media confidentiality, limit unauthorized sessions, and preserve acceptable call quality.
questions.prompt: Which design is MOST appropriate?

choices.A: Protect signaling and media with appropriate secure protocols, enforce sessions at a voice-aware boundary control, and apply quality-of-service policy
choices.B: Encrypt signaling only because media streams contain no sensitive information
choices.C: Place all voice endpoints directly on the Internet to avoid boundary latency
choices.D: Use the data network without segmentation, session controls, or traffic prioritization

questions.explanation: Voice security requires protection of both signaling and media, controlled traversal of trust boundaries, and availability measures appropriate to real-time traffic. Signaling-only protection leaves conversations exposed, while direct exposure and an unsegmented, uncontrolled design increase attack and quality risks.

questions.competency: IV.D — Secure Communication Channels
questions.skill: Securing third-party remote administrative access
questions.performanceIndicator: Design a monitored, least-privilege remote access path for an external party
questions.scenarioContext: A utility must allow a maintenance vendor to administer one internal appliance during approved service windows. The utility requires individual accountability, minimal network exposure, and rapid revocation when the engagement ends.
questions.prompt: Which approach BEST meets these requirements?

choices.A: Provide a shared VPN account with access to the full operations network
choices.B: Use individually authenticated access through a monitored gateway, restricted to the target and approved times
choices.C: Publish the appliance's management interface directly to the Internet
choices.D: Allow the vendor to reuse an employee's permanent remote-access credentials

questions.explanation: An individually authenticated, monitored gateway with target and time restrictions provides accountability, least privilege, and straightforward revocation. Shared or borrowed credentials defeat attribution, broad VPN access exceeds need, and direct Internet exposure unnecessarily increases attack surface.

questions.competency: IV.D — Secure Communication Channels
questions.skill: Securing virtual meeting access and shared content
questions.performanceIndicator: Apply access, confidentiality, and governance controls to external collaboration
questions.scenarioContext: An engineering firm will discuss confidential designs in video conferences with invited external partners. Previous public meeting links were forwarded to unintended participants, and recordings were retained without clear ownership.
questions.prompt: What should the security manager recommend FIRST?

choices.A: Use authenticated invitations, controlled admission, restricted sharing, and an approved recording-retention policy
choices.B: Post one reusable meeting link publicly so partners can join easily
choices.C: Rely on participants to identify unexpected attendees after the meeting
choices.D: Permit unrestricted local recordings because storage is outside the network path

questions.explanation: Authenticated invitations, admission controls, sharing restrictions, and governed recording retention address unauthorized attendance, content exposure, and information lifecycle risk together. Public reusable links, after-the-fact identification, and unrestricted recording do not provide preventive or accountable protection.

questions.competency: V.A — Access Control Fundamentals and Authentication Strategy
questions.skill: Selecting authentication controls appropriate to elevated administrative risk
questions.performanceIndicator: Differentiate identification, authentication, authorization, and accountability when protecting privileged access
questions.scenarioContext: A regional utility permits administrators to manage critical servers from corporate workstations. A stolen administrator password recently allowed an attacker to begin an interactive sign-in, although monitoring stopped the session before changes were made.
questions.prompt: Which change would MOST directly reduce the likelihood that another stolen password could be used to establish an administrative session?

choices.A: Require a second authentication factor that is resistant to credential replay
choices.B: Shorten the inactivity timeout for all established administrative sessions
choices.C: Record every privileged command in a centralized activity log
choices.D: Reconfirm each administrator's assigned privileges every quarter

questions.explanation: A replay-resistant second factor most directly prevents possession of a stolen password from being sufficient to establish a session. A shorter timeout limits exposure after a session exists, and command logging improves accountability after access. Quarterly privilege reviews address authorization and entitlement appropriateness, not the immediate authentication weakness.

questions.competency: V.A — Access Control Fundamentals and Authentication Strategy
questions.skill: Preserving individual accountability for shared operational tasks
questions.performanceIndicator: Apply IAAA principles to administrative access design
questions.scenarioContext: A manufacturing plant uses one shared maintenance account because several technicians must respond quickly to equipment failures. The account has broad permissions, and investigators cannot determine which technician made a recent configuration change.
questions.prompt: What is the BEST way to preserve rapid response while establishing accountability?

choices.A: Keep the shared account and require technicians to record their names in a paper log
choices.B: Issue individually attributable accounts and grant the required maintenance role to each technician
choices.C: Change the shared account password after every maintenance event
choices.D: Allow the supervisor to disclose the shared password only when an outage occurs

questions.explanation: Individual accounts tied to a maintenance role preserve operational access while making activity attributable to a specific technician. A paper log can be incomplete or falsified, and rotating a shared password does not identify the person using it. Supervisor-controlled disclosure limits availability but still leaves activity associated with the same shared identity.

questions.competency: V.A — Access Control Fundamentals and Authentication Strategy
questions.skill: Designing secure session invalidation after a credential event
questions.performanceIndicator: Recognize the distinction between credential reset and active-session control
questions.scenarioContext: An online services organization resets a user's password after confirming account compromise. The application uses long-lived session tokens that remain valid after a password change.
questions.prompt: Which action should the organization take FIRST to contain continued use of the compromised account?

choices.A: Reduce the minimum password age for the affected account
choices.B: Invalidate the user's existing sessions and authentication tokens
choices.C: Add the user's address to a security notification list
choices.D: Review the user's business role at the next certification cycle

questions.explanation: Invalidating active sessions and tokens immediately removes the attacker's continuing authenticated state. Changing password policy does not terminate tokens already issued. Notifications may support response communications, and a later role review may identify excessive privileges, but neither contains the active session first.

questions.competency: V.A — Access Control Fundamentals and Authentication Strategy
questions.skill: Identifying independent authentication factors in an MFA design
questions.performanceIndicator: Classify knowledge, possession, and inherence factors accurately
questions.prompt: Which TWO combinations provide two different authentication factor categories? Select 2 of the 5 options below.

choices.A: A password and a memorized personal identification number
choices.B: A hardware security key and a fingerprint
choices.C: A passphrase and the answer to a knowledge-based question
choices.D: A smart card and a personal identification number
choices.E: A fingerprint and facial recognition

questions.explanation: A hardware key plus a fingerprint combines possession and inherence, while a smart card plus a personal identification number combines possession and knowledge. A password with a personal identification number and a passphrase with a knowledge-based answer each use two knowledge credentials. A fingerprint and facial recognition are both inherence factors, so using both does not create factor-category diversity.

questions.competency: V.A — Access Control Fundamentals and Authentication Strategy
questions.skill: Protecting credentials stored by an authentication system
questions.performanceIndicator: Select credential storage controls that limit offline password recovery
questions.scenarioContext: A nonprofit is replacing an application that stores user passwords with a general-purpose fast hash. The security architect wants a design that limits the value of a stolen credential database and makes large-scale offline guessing more expensive.
questions.prompt: Which approach BEST meets the architect's objective?

choices.A: Encrypt all passwords with one reversible key stored on the application server
choices.B: Store each password with a unique salt using an adaptive password-hashing function
choices.C: Apply the same random salt to every password before using the existing fast hash
choices.D: Encode each password and restrict read access to the credential table

questions.explanation: A unique salt defeats precomputed comparisons across accounts, and an adaptive password-hashing function raises the cost of each offline guess. Reversible encryption creates dependence on protecting a decryption key. One common salt still permits efficient comparison across accounts, while encoding provides no cryptographic protection even if database permissions are useful defense in depth.

questions.competency: V.B — Federated Identity and Authentication Systems
questions.skill: Selecting a federation protocol for browser-based enterprise SSO
questions.performanceIndicator: Match SAML roles and assertions to cross-domain authentication requirements
questions.scenarioContext: A university wants employees to use their institutional credentials to access a browser-based human resources service operated by an external provider. The university must remain responsible for authenticating its employees, and the provider must consume an assertion to create the service session.
questions.prompt: Which architecture BEST satisfies this requirement?

choices.A: The university acts as a SAML identity provider and the external service acts as a service provider
choices.B: The external service acts as an OAuth resource server and issues university passwords
choices.C: The university acts as a SAML service provider and delegates authentication to the external service
choices.D: The external service uses an authorization code as proof of the employee's identity without an identity assertion

questions.explanation: In this federation pattern, the university authenticates the employee as the identity provider and sends a signed SAML assertion to the service provider. Reversing those roles would transfer authentication responsibility to the external service. OAuth resource access and an authorization code alone do not provide the requested SAML identity assertion and should not require the provider to issue university passwords.

questions.competency: V.B — Federated Identity and Authentication Systems
questions.skill: Distinguishing delegated authorization from authentication
questions.performanceIndicator: Explain why OAuth alone does not establish an end-user identity
questions.scenarioContext: A development team uses OAuth so a scheduling application can read a user's calendar through an API. The team now proposes treating the OAuth access token by itself as proof that a particular user authenticated to the scheduling application.
questions.prompt: What is the MOST important flaw in the proposal?

choices.A: OAuth access tokens can be used only with applications inside one security domain
choices.B: OAuth delegates access to a resource but does not, by itself, define an authentication assertion for the client
choices.C: OAuth requires the resource owner to disclose credentials directly to every client application
choices.D: OAuth prevents a resource server from limiting the scope of delegated access

questions.explanation: OAuth is an authorization framework for delegated resource access; possession of an access token alone is not a standardized assertion that the client authenticated a particular end user. OpenID Connect adds an identity layer for that purpose. OAuth can operate across trust domains, avoids routine credential disclosure to clients in appropriate flows, and supports scoped access.

questions.competency: V.B — Federated Identity and Authentication Systems
questions.skill: Using OpenID Connect for application sign-in
questions.performanceIndicator: Identify the security purpose of an ID token in an OpenID Connect flow
questions.scenarioContext: A media organization is implementing sign-in for several modern web and mobile applications. Its authorization server already supports OAuth, and the applications require standardized claims about the authenticated user.
questions.prompt: Which addition MOST directly provides the required authentication information?

choices.A: OpenID Connect with a validated ID token intended for the client
choices.B: A broader OAuth access-token scope for each protected API
choices.C: A refresh token stored as the user's permanent identity record
choices.D: A resource-server response containing the client's secret

questions.explanation: OpenID Connect adds authentication to OAuth-based flows and provides an ID token containing claims for the client, subject to validation of issuer, audience, signature, and related properties. Expanding API scopes changes authorization, not authentication. Refresh tokens obtain new tokens and are not identity records, while a client secret must not be exposed by a resource server.

questions.competency: V.B — Federated Identity and Authentication Systems
questions.skill: Establishing controls for a third-party identity trust
questions.performanceIndicator: Identify governance and technical prerequisites for federation across trust boundaries
questions.scenarioContext: A logistics company will trust a partner's identity service so partner personnel can access a shared shipment portal. The parties want to reduce unauthorized access caused by stale partner accounts and improperly accepted assertions.
questions.prompt: Which TWO controls are MOST important before enabling the federation? Select 2 of the 5 options below.

choices.A: Define assurance, lifecycle, incident, and account-termination responsibilities in the trust agreement
choices.B: Validate assertion signatures, issuer, audience, and validity period at the relying service
choices.C: Permit all partner identities to receive one common local administrator role
choices.D: Retain partner accounts indefinitely so past shipment records remain attributable
choices.E: Allow the partner to select any claim names without an agreed mapping

questions.explanation: A federation requires both governance of the identity lifecycle and rigorous validation of the assertions crossing the trust boundary. The trust agreement establishes who must provision, disable, notify, and respond, while signature, issuer, audience, and time validation prevents acceptance of forged or misdirected assertions. Broad administrative access, indefinite active accounts, and undefined claim mappings undermine least privilege and reliable authorization.

questions.competency: V.B — Federated Identity and Authentication Systems
questions.skill: Managing centralized SSO failure and compromise risk
questions.performanceIndicator: Balance usability benefits of SSO with resilience and containment controls
questions.scenarioContext: A global retailer plans to use one cloud identity service for single sign-on to most workforce applications. Executives are concerned that an identity-service outage or compromise could affect many business functions at once.
questions.prompt: Which design response BEST addresses the concentration of risk without abandoning SSO?

choices.A: Give each employee a shared emergency account accepted by all applications
choices.B: Implement resilient identity-service architecture and tightly controlled break-glass access for critical systems
choices.C: Allow every application to retain a permanent copy of the employee's primary password
choices.D: Disable centralized logging so a compromise cannot alter all authentication records

questions.explanation: Resilient identity services reduce availability risk, and narrowly scoped, monitored break-glass access supports continuity when federation is unavailable. Shared emergency accounts weaken accountability. Distributing reusable passwords expands credential exposure, and disabling centralized logging removes detection evidence rather than containing identity-provider risk.

questions.competency: V.C — Authorization Mechanisms
questions.skill: Selecting ABAC for context-sensitive access decisions
questions.performanceIndicator: Match an authorization model to user, resource, action, and environmental attributes
questions.scenarioContext: A research consortium shares documents among employees, visiting scientists, and contractors. Access depends on project membership, document sensitivity, contract status, geographic location, and whether the request occurs during an approved collaboration period. The combinations change frequently.
questions.prompt: Which access control model BEST supports these requirements with the least role proliferation?

choices.A: Attribute-based access control
choices.B: Discretionary access control
choices.C: Mandatory access control based only on fixed security labels
choices.D: Role-based access control using a separate role for every possible combination

questions.explanation: ABAC evaluates policies using subject, resource, action, and environmental attributes, making it well suited to dynamic combinations such as project, contract, location, and time. DAC places decisions with resource owners and may be inconsistent. Label-based MAC does not naturally express all listed conditions, while encoding every combination as an RBAC role creates role explosion.

questions.competency: V.C — Authorization Mechanisms
questions.skill: Differentiating policy decision and enforcement functions
questions.performanceIndicator: Place access-evaluation and request-interception responsibilities correctly
questions.scenarioContext: An insurance company is centralizing authorization. One component will evaluate policy using identity and resource attributes, while a gateway in front of each application will intercept requests and carry out the resulting allow-or-deny decision.
questions.prompt: How should the two components be classified?

choices.A: The evaluator is the policy enforcement point, and the gateway is the policy decision point
choices.B: The evaluator is the policy decision point, and the gateway is the policy enforcement point
choices.C: Both components are policy decision points because both participate in authorization
choices.D: Both components are policy enforcement points because neither authenticates the user

questions.explanation: The policy decision point evaluates applicable policy and returns an authorization decision. The policy enforcement point intercepts the access request and enforces that decision at the resource boundary. Participation in one authorization flow does not make both components the same, and authentication is separate from these authorization roles.

questions.competency: V.C — Authorization Mechanisms
questions.skill: Applying mandatory access control to classified information
questions.performanceIndicator: Recognize centrally administered label-based authorization
questions.scenarioContext: A government agency requires documents and users to carry formal security labels. Individual document owners must not be able to grant access at their discretion, and a centrally defined policy must govern interactions between clearances and classifications.
questions.prompt: Which authorization model is MOST appropriate?

choices.A: Discretionary access control
choices.B: Role-based access control
choices.C: Mandatory access control
choices.D: Risk-based access control

questions.explanation: Mandatory access control uses centrally administered labels and rules, preventing resource owners from independently changing access to classified information. DAC explicitly gives owners discretion. RBAC organizes permissions around job functions but does not inherently enforce clearance and classification labels, while risk-based access changes decisions according to assessed contextual risk.

questions.competency: V.C — Authorization Mechanisms
questions.skill: Distinguishing rule-based controls from role assignments
questions.performanceIndicator: Select an access model for globally applied conditions independent of job function
questions.scenarioContext: A financial services firm assigns application permissions through job roles. It also needs a centrally managed condition that blocks all remote access to a sensitive function outside approved hours, regardless of the user's role.
questions.prompt: Which mechanism BEST expresses the additional condition?

choices.A: A discretionary access list maintained separately by each data owner
choices.B: A rule-based access control rule evaluated for every request
choices.C: A new permanent role for every employee who works during approved hours
choices.D: A mandatory classification label assigned to the time of day

questions.explanation: A centrally applied rule can evaluate time and connection context for every request independently of the user's role. Owner-maintained discretionary lists would fragment enforcement. Creating permanent roles for a changing time condition misuses RBAC and increases administration, while a classification label is not the appropriate representation of time-based access.

questions.competency: V.C — Authorization Mechanisms
questions.skill: Using adaptive risk signals without discarding baseline authorization
questions.performanceIndicator: Apply risk-based access control as a contextual layer over entitlements
questions.scenarioContext: A payment processor wants ordinarily permitted account access to receive additional scrutiny when sign-in behavior is anomalous, the device is unmanaged, or the transaction is unusually sensitive. Existing job entitlements must remain the baseline.
questions.prompt: What is the BEST authorization strategy?

choices.A: Replace all job entitlements with resource-owner discretion
choices.B: Apply risk-based decisions that can require step-up authentication or deny high-risk requests
choices.C: Grant permanent elevated roles to users who frequently trigger risk checks
choices.D: Approve access solely from the sensitivity label without considering request context

questions.explanation: Risk-based access can combine baseline entitlement with signals such as device posture, behavior, location, and transaction sensitivity, then allow, challenge, or deny the request. Owner discretion does not provide consistent adaptive decisions. Permanent elevation rewards risky patterns and violates least privilege, while relying only on a label ignores the requested contextual analysis.

questions.competency: V.D — The Identity and Access Provisioning Lifecycle
questions.skill: Prioritizing deprovisioning after workforce termination
questions.performanceIndicator: Coordinate authoritative employment status with timely access revocation
questions.scenarioContext: A sales employee with access to customer records is being terminated at the end of a meeting. Human resources, the manager, and the identity team know the scheduled time. Several cloud applications receive accounts from the central identity platform.
questions.prompt: Which action is MOST important for the identity team to coordinate?

choices.A: Disable access at the effective termination time and propagate revocation to connected services
choices.B: Wait for the next monthly entitlement review before changing the account
choices.C: Remove the employee from the office directory but retain all application sessions
choices.D: Transfer the employee's password to the manager for business continuity

questions.explanation: Revocation aligned with the effective termination time closes the access window while respecting the coordinated personnel process, and propagation addresses downstream services and sessions. A monthly review is too late. Directory removal alone may not revoke application access, and transferring a personal password breaks accountability and proper credential handling.

questions.competency: V.D — The Identity and Access Provisioning Lifecycle
questions.skill: Managing access when an employee changes roles
questions.performanceIndicator: Prevent privilege accumulation during internal transfers
questions.scenarioContext: An employee moves from procurement to accounts payable. The organization commonly adds the new department's permissions immediately but leaves removal of old permissions for a later cleanup project.
questions.prompt: Which lifecycle control BEST prevents privilege accumulation in this situation?

choices.A: Copy the access of a highly experienced accounts-payable employee
choices.B: Treat the transfer as a controlled remove-and-add event based on approved role requirements
choices.C: Retain procurement access in case the employee assists the former team
choices.D: Allow the employee to choose which legacy permissions remain useful

questions.explanation: A role transfer should trigger removal of access no longer required and addition of access approved for the new role, avoiding entitlement accumulation. Copying another employee can reproduce excessive or exceptional privileges. Keeping old access by default and letting the user choose both bypass business ownership, least privilege, and separation-of-duties review.

questions.competency: V.D — The Identity and Access Provisioning Lifecycle
questions.skill: Designing just-in-time privileged access
questions.performanceIndicator: Identify controls that bound and attribute temporary elevation
questions.scenarioContext: A hospital wants database administrators to use standard accounts for daily work and receive elevated production privileges only for approved maintenance. The privileges should not remain after the work window.
questions.prompt: Which TWO controls BEST implement this just-in-time objective? Select 2 of the 5 options below.

choices.A: Require an approved request tied to the administrator's individual identity
choices.B: Automatically expire the elevated entitlement at the end of the authorized period
choices.C: Publish one standing privileged password to the entire database team
choices.D: Convert every administrator's standard account into a permanent privileged account
choices.E: Allow administrators to renew elevation indefinitely without additional approval

questions.explanation: An individually attributable approval and automatic expiration provide the essential governance and time boundary for just-in-time privilege. A shared password weakens accountability. Permanent elevation defeats the objective, and unlimited self-renewal can turn temporary access into standing privilege without renewed business authorization.

questions.competency: V.D — The Identity and Access Provisioning Lifecycle
questions.skill: Conducting effective entitlement reviews with accountable ownership
questions.performanceIndicator: Structure access certification so informed owners validate business need
questions.scenarioContext: A pharmaceutical company finds that managers approve quarterly access lists without understanding cryptic group names. The identity team wants future reviews to produce meaningful decisions about continued business need.
questions.prompt: Which improvement would MOST increase the effectiveness of the reviews?

choices.A: Provide reviewers with entitlement descriptions, user context, ownership, and risk information
choices.B: Ask the identity operations team to approve every entitlement on behalf of managers
choices.C: Automatically retain access whenever a reviewer does not respond by the deadline
choices.D: Show only the date each technical group was created to simplify the review

questions.explanation: Reviewers need intelligible entitlement descriptions, relevant user and role context, accountable ownership, and risk information to decide whether access remains justified. Identity operations usually cannot attest to each user's business need. Default retention for nonresponse preserves potentially inappropriate access, and group-creation dates do not explain permissions or current necessity.

questions.competency: V.D — The Identity and Access Provisioning Lifecycle
questions.skill: Controlling service-account provisioning and ownership
questions.performanceIndicator: Apply lifecycle governance to nonhuman identities
questions.scenarioContext: A transportation company discovers hundreds of service accounts with no recorded owner, no expiration or review date, and privileges accumulated across retired applications. Some credentials are embedded in automation scripts.
questions.prompt: What should the identity governance team do FIRST?

choices.A: Delete every service account immediately, including those used by active systems
choices.B: Inventory usage and dependencies, assign accountable owners, and validate each account's required privileges
choices.C: Give all service accounts the same enterprise role to simplify administration
choices.D: Exclude nonhuman identities from lifecycle controls because no employee signs in with them

questions.explanation: The team must first understand dependencies and establish ownership before safely remediating nonhuman identities; it can then remove unused accounts, reduce privileges, rotate exposed credentials, and define review and retirement controls. Immediate deletion could disrupt critical services. A common broad role increases exposure, and service accounts require lifecycle governance precisely because unmanaged nonhuman access can persist unnoticed.

questions.competency: VI.A — Assessment, Test, and Audit Strategy
questions.skill: Selecting an independent assessment approach for a high-risk service
questions.performanceIndicator: Choose an assessment approach that provides appropriate independence and assurance
questions.scenarioContext: A regional payment processor is preparing to renew a major client contract. The internal security team designed and operates the controls protecting the service, and the client requires objective assurance about their effectiveness.
questions.prompt: Which assessment approach would provide the MOST credible assurance to the client?

choices.A: Have the control owners complete a new self-assessment questionnaire.
choices.B: Assign an internal administrator to verify the configurations informally.
choices.C: Engage an independent qualified assessor to test the controls against an agreed scope.
choices.D: Ask the client to rely on the processor's existing security policies.

questions.explanation: An independent qualified assessor offers the strongest objectivity when external stakeholders need credible assurance. A self-assessment or informal administrator review lacks sufficient independence, while policies describe intended behavior but do not demonstrate operating effectiveness.

questions.competency: VI.A — Assessment, Test, and Audit Strategy
questions.skill: Defining risk-based audit scope
questions.performanceIndicator: Prioritize audit coverage using business impact, threat exposure, and prior findings
questions.scenarioContext: A security manager must plan an internal audit with limited staff. A customer portal processes sensitive records and has unresolved prior findings, while several low-impact internal tools have stable control histories.
questions.prompt: What should the manager do FIRST when establishing the audit scope?

choices.A: Give every system equal testing time to demonstrate uniform treatment.
choices.B: Prioritize systems according to business impact, exposure, and unresolved findings.
choices.C: Limit the audit to controls that can be tested automatically.
choices.D: Exclude systems previously audited so the team can maximize new coverage.

questions.explanation: A risk-based scope directs limited assurance resources toward the systems and controls whose failure would matter most. Equal allocation ignores differing risk, automation should not define scope, and prior audits do not justify excluding systems with significant or unresolved risk.

questions.competency: VI.A — Assessment, Test, and Audit Strategy
questions.skill: Preserving separation between audit and remediation responsibilities
questions.performanceIndicator: Maintain auditor objectivity while enabling management to address findings
questions.scenarioContext: During an internal audit, an auditor discovers that privileged access reviews are not being completed. The application owner asks the auditor to redesign and operate the review process before the final report is issued.
questions.prompt: What is the auditor's BEST response?

choices.A: Design and operate the control so the finding can be closed immediately.
choices.B: Remove the finding because management has expressed an intent to remediate it.
choices.C: Describe the issue and criteria, while leaving control ownership and remediation to management.
choices.D: Delay all reporting until the application owner independently discovers the same issue.

questions.explanation: The auditor should report the condition and preserve independence by leaving control design, ownership, and operation to management. Operating the control creates a self-review threat, management intent alone does not resolve the finding, and withholding a valid finding undermines the audit.

questions.competency: VI.A — Assessment, Test, and Audit Strategy
questions.skill: Establishing a controlled penetration test engagement
questions.performanceIndicator: Identify governance prerequisites that authorize testing and limit operational risk
questions.scenarioContext: A university has approved a third-party penetration test of its student services environment. Testing could affect shared infrastructure and systems managed by an external hosting provider.
questions.prompt: Which TWO items should be formally established before active testing begins? Select 2 of the 5 options below.

choices.A: Written authorization and clearly defined rules of engagement.
choices.B: A guarantee that every vulnerability in the environment will be found.
choices.C: Scope boundaries, escalation contacts, and permitted testing windows.
choices.D: Immediate public disclosure of all discovered vulnerabilities.
choices.E: Permanent administrative credentials for every production system.

questions.explanation: Written authorization and rules of engagement establish legal and operational permission, while scope boundaries, contacts, and testing windows constrain risk and enable incident coordination. Complete discovery cannot be guaranteed, public disclosure is not a prerequisite, and unrestricted permanent credentials would create unnecessary exposure.

questions.competency: VI.A — Assessment, Test, and Audit Strategy
questions.skill: Interpreting the assurance provided by a SOC report
questions.performanceIndicator: Evaluate whether third-party assurance evidence matches the period and controls under review
questions.scenarioContext: A cloud service provider supplies a report describing whether specified controls were suitably designed and operated effectively over a defined six-month period. A customer wants assurance covering its fiscal year and its own complementary controls.
questions.prompt: What should the customer security manager do NEXT?

choices.A: Accept the report as proof that all customer responsibilities were performed.
choices.B: Confirm the report's scope and period, review exceptions, and evaluate complementary user-entity controls.
choices.C: Treat the report as a vulnerability scan of the provider's entire environment.
choices.D: Replace all internal vendor oversight with the provider's management assertion.

questions.explanation: Third-party assurance must be evaluated against the customer's required scope and period, including noted exceptions and complementary controls assigned to the customer. The report does not prove customer control performance, represent a universal vulnerability scan, or eliminate vendor oversight responsibilities.

questions.competency: VI.A — Assessment, Test, and Audit Strategy
questions.skill: Coordinating regulatory and internal audit work
questions.performanceIndicator: Use existing assurance evidence efficiently without compromising audit objectives
questions.scenarioContext: A regulated utility expects an external compliance audit shortly after its annual internal audit. Both engagements cover several of the same access-control processes, but the external auditor retains responsibility for its own conclusions.
questions.prompt: Which strategy BEST reduces duplication while preserving assurance?

choices.A: Cancel the internal audit because the external audit will cover similar controls.
choices.B: Let the control owners choose which evidence the external auditor may see.
choices.C: Align schedules and evidence collection, document internal work quality, and allow the external auditor to determine reliance.
choices.D: Require the external auditor to adopt every internal conclusion without additional procedures.

questions.explanation: Coordinated scheduling and reusable, well-documented evidence can reduce burden, while the external auditor independently decides whether and how much to rely on internal work. Canceling internal assurance may leave governance gaps, selective evidence threatens completeness, and compulsory reliance undermines external independence.

questions.competency: VI.B — Conducting Security Control Testing
questions.skill: Distinguishing vulnerability assessment from penetration testing
questions.performanceIndicator: Select the test that answers whether identified weaknesses can be exploited to achieve an objective
questions.scenarioContext: An engineering firm has received a scanner report listing missing patches and insecure configurations. Leadership now wants to know whether an attacker could combine those weaknesses to reach restricted design files.
questions.prompt: Which activity would BEST answer leadership's question?

choices.A: A penetration test with an authorized objective of reaching the restricted files.
choices.B: A second vulnerability scan using the same signatures.
choices.C: A policy review focused on patch-management documentation.
choices.D: A count of devices represented in the asset inventory.

questions.explanation: A penetration test attempts controlled exploitation and can demonstrate whether weaknesses can be chained to achieve the defined objective. A vulnerability scan identifies potential weaknesses but does not establish exploitability, while policy and inventory reviews address different assurance questions.

questions.competency: VI.B — Conducting Security Control Testing
questions.skill: Using purple-team collaboration to improve detection controls
questions.performanceIndicator: Choose a testing model that combines realistic attack activity with defensive learning
questions.scenarioContext: A media company wants to determine why its monitoring rules miss certain credential-abuse behaviors. Leadership wants offensive testers and defenders to share observations during the exercise so detections can be tuned and retested immediately.
questions.prompt: Which team structure BEST supports this objective?

choices.A: A red team operating without any defined scope or defender contact.
choices.B: A blue team reviewing alerts without simulated adversary activity.
choices.C: A purple-team exercise that coordinates offensive actions and defensive validation.
choices.D: An audit committee reviewing only the final annual metrics.

questions.explanation: A purple-team approach deliberately connects offensive techniques with defensive observation, tuning, and retesting. An isolated red or blue team provides only one side of the feedback loop, and an audit committee's metric review cannot reproduce or validate technical detection behavior.

questions.competency: VI.B — Conducting Security Control Testing
questions.skill: Selecting static and dynamic application testing methods
questions.performanceIndicator: Match code and runtime testing methods to the evidence required
questions.scenarioContext: Before releasing a new claims application, a development security lead must identify unsafe code paths and also observe failures that appear only while the application is executing.
questions.prompt: Which testing strategy provides the MOST complete coverage of these objectives?

choices.A: Use only static analysis because runtime behavior is outside the assessment scope.
choices.B: Combine static analysis of code with dynamic testing of the running application.
choices.C: Use only network discovery because it evaluates application logic directly.
choices.D: Review user training records instead of testing the application.

questions.explanation: Static analysis can expose weaknesses in source or compiled code paths, while dynamic testing observes behavior in an executing application. Combining them addresses complementary evidence needs. Network discovery does not directly evaluate application logic, and training records do not test software controls.

questions.competency: VI.B — Conducting Security Control Testing
questions.skill: Validating transaction integrity and monitoring through synthetic activity
questions.performanceIndicator: Identify controlled tests that verify both business processing and security telemetry
questions.scenarioContext: An online retailer must verify that a fraud control blocks a prohibited transaction pattern and that the attempted transaction creates the expected alert without using a real customer account.
questions.prompt: Which TWO actions are MOST appropriate? Select 2 of the 5 options below.

choices.A: Execute a preauthorized synthetic transaction using a controlled test identity.
choices.B: Disable alerting during the test to prevent misleading evidence.
choices.C: Confirm the expected rejection and correlate the generated event with the security alert.
choices.D: Use an uninformed customer's account so the scenario appears realistic.
choices.E: Assume the control works because its configuration matches the documented standard.

questions.explanation: A controlled synthetic transaction tests the business process without exposing a real customer, and correlating the outcome with the alert verifies both prevention and detection. Disabling alerting removes required evidence, using a customer account is inappropriate, and configuration conformity alone does not prove operational effectiveness.

questions.competency: VI.B — Conducting Security Control Testing
questions.skill: Evaluating test coverage against misuse cases and interfaces
questions.performanceIndicator: Identify material gaps in control test coverage
questions.scenarioContext: A test report for a funds-transfer service shows full coverage of approved user workflows. It does not test malformed requests at an external interface or attempts by authorized users to exceed their transaction limits.
questions.prompt: What is the MOST significant concern with the report?

choices.A: The testing omitted interface abuse and misuse cases, so stated coverage may overestimate assurance.
choices.B: The test team should have measured only the number of successful transactions.
choices.C: Approved workflow coverage makes negative testing unnecessary.
choices.D: The service cannot be tested until every possible input has been enumerated.

questions.explanation: Coverage of normal workflows does not demonstrate resilience against malformed interface input or authorized-user misuse. Transaction counts alone do not address negative paths, approved flows do not replace misuse testing, and exhaustive enumeration of every input is neither necessary nor practical for risk-based assurance.

questions.competency: VI.B — Conducting Security Control Testing
questions.skill: Scoping a breach and attack simulation safely
questions.performanceIndicator: Use threat-informed automated simulation without confusing it with unrestricted penetration testing
questions.scenarioContext: A manufacturing company plans recurring automated simulations of selected adversary techniques against production security controls. Operations leaders are concerned that the activity could interrupt industrial support services.
questions.prompt: What is the BEST way to proceed?

choices.A: Run every available technique without notice to maximize realism.
choices.B: Define approved techniques, safety constraints, monitoring, and rollback procedures before execution.
choices.C: Replace the simulation with a review of written security policies only.
choices.D: Allow the simulation platform to expand its own scope whenever it finds a weakness.

questions.explanation: Threat-informed simulation can validate controls repeatedly, but production use requires explicit scope, safeguards, observation, and recovery procedures. Unrestricted or self-expanding tests create unacceptable operational risk, while policy review alone cannot demonstrate how technical controls respond to simulated techniques.

questions.competency: VI.C — Collecting Process Data and Reporting Results
questions.skill: Selecting evidence of account management control performance
questions.performanceIndicator: Collect records that demonstrate timely deprovisioning rather than documented intent
questions.scenarioContext: An auditor is testing whether user access is removed promptly after employment termination. Human resources policy requires removal within one business day.
questions.prompt: Which evidence would BEST demonstrate the control's operating effectiveness?

choices.A: A copy of the approved termination policy by itself.
choices.B: A sample linking termination timestamps to account-disablement records and documented exceptions.
choices.C: A current organizational chart showing reporting relationships.
choices.D: A statement from the help desk that requests are usually handled quickly.

questions.explanation: Timestamped records matched across the triggering and deprovisioning processes provide evidence that the control operated within the required period, while exceptions reveal failures. Policy proves design intent, and an organizational chart or general statement does not substantiate actual performance.

questions.competency: VI.C — Collecting Process Data and Reporting Results
questions.skill: Differentiating key performance and key risk indicators
questions.performanceIndicator: Interpret process metrics according to whether they measure execution or exposure
questions.scenarioContext: A security steering committee reviews two monthly measures: the percentage of critical patches installed within the required service level and the number of internet-facing critical vulnerabilities older than that service level.
questions.prompt: How should these measures be classified?

choices.A: Both are financial audit measures because they concern resource allocation.
choices.B: The installation percentage is a performance indicator, while the overdue exposure count is a risk indicator.
choices.C: The installation percentage is a risk indicator, while the overdue exposure count is a performance indicator.
choices.D: Neither is useful because security controls cannot be evaluated with metrics.

questions.explanation: The installation percentage measures how well the patching process meets its target, making it a key performance indicator. The count of overdue exposed vulnerabilities signals current risk exposure, making it a key risk indicator. Both measures can support control assessment when definitions and data quality are sound.

questions.competency: VI.C — Collecting Process Data and Reporting Results
questions.skill: Verifying backup recoverability
questions.performanceIndicator: Use restoration evidence to evaluate whether backups support recovery objectives
questions.scenarioContext: A hospital's backup dashboard shows that scheduled jobs completed successfully for the past quarter. The audit objective is to determine whether critical records can be recovered within approved recovery targets.
questions.prompt: What additional evidence is MOST important?

choices.A: Documented restoration tests showing data integrity and recovery times for representative systems.
choices.B: The total storage capacity purchased for the backup environment.
choices.C: A list of employees permitted to view the backup dashboard.
choices.D: A vendor brochure describing general backup features.

questions.explanation: Successful job status shows that backup operations ran, but restoration testing demonstrates recoverability, integrity, and alignment with recovery targets. Capacity and dashboard access may matter to other controls, while marketing material provides no evidence that this organization's data can be restored.

questions.competency: VI.C — Collecting Process Data and Reporting Results
questions.skill: Assessing security awareness effectiveness
questions.performanceIndicator: Combine outcome and process data to evaluate whether training changes behavior
questions.scenarioContext: A public agency reports that nearly all personnel completed annual security awareness training. The security manager must determine whether the program is improving recognition and reporting of suspicious messages.
questions.prompt: Which TWO measures would provide the MOST useful evidence of effectiveness? Select 2 of the 5 options below.

choices.A: Results from controlled simulations, analyzed by role and trend over time.
choices.B: The number of training slides included in the annual course.
choices.C: Timeliness and quality of employee reports from simulations or validated events.
choices.D: The amount originally budgeted for training development.
choices.E: The seniority of the manager who approved the course.

questions.explanation: Simulation results and the timeliness and quality of reporting measure observable behavior tied to the program's objective. Slide count, budget, and approver seniority are administrative facts that do not show whether personnel can recognize and report suspicious activity effectively.

questions.competency: VI.C — Collecting Process Data and Reporting Results
questions.skill: Reporting test findings according to risk and root cause
questions.performanceIndicator: Produce actionable reporting that connects evidence, impact, ownership, and remediation
questions.scenarioContext: A disaster recovery exercise missed the recovery time objective for two critical services. The test team found that an outdated dependency map caused the restoration sequence to fail, and service owners have proposed corrective actions.
questions.prompt: Which reporting approach would BEST support management action?

choices.A: Report only that the exercise failed, without identifying affected objectives.
choices.B: List every test log entry chronologically and let executives determine significance.
choices.C: Describe the evidence, business impact, root cause, responsible owners, and time-bound remediation plan.
choices.D: Remove the result because corrective actions have already been proposed.

questions.explanation: An actionable report connects verified evidence to business impact and root cause, then identifies accountability and remediation timing. A bare failure statement lacks decision context, raw logs overwhelm the audience, and a proposed action does not erase the observed control deficiency.

questions.competency: VI.C — Collecting Process Data and Reporting Results
questions.skill: Resolving contradictory audit evidence
questions.performanceIndicator: Corroborate evidence and expand testing before reaching an audit conclusion
questions.scenarioContext: During a third-party audit, management approval records indicate that privileged accounts were reviewed quarterly. System logs for the same period suggest that several accounts remained active after their owners changed roles.
questions.prompt: What should the audit lead do FIRST?

choices.A: Accept the approval records because signed evidence takes precedence over technical data.
choices.B: Conclude immediately that management intentionally falsified the records.
choices.C: Reconcile the populations and timestamps, obtain corroborating evidence, and expand the sample if warranted.
choices.D: Discard both sources and report that the control cannot be assessed.

questions.explanation: Contradictory evidence should be reconciled by validating scope, timing, and data sources, then gathering corroboration and extending testing as risk warrants. Neither signed records nor logs should be accepted uncritically, intent should not be inferred without evidence, and the discrepancy itself justifies further assessment rather than abandonment.

questions.competency: VII.A — Investigations, Logging, and Configuration Management
questions.skill: Preserving volatile digital evidence during incident investigation
questions.performanceIndicator: Choose an evidence-collection sequence that preserves probative value and supports later analysis
questions.scenarioContext: A security analyst is investigating a compromised application server that remains powered on and connected to an isolated forensic network. The server contains active processes, network sessions, encryption keys in memory, and persistent storage that can be imaged.
questions.prompt: Which action should the analyst take FIRST to preserve the most time-sensitive evidence?

choices.A: Create a bit-for-bit image of each persistent storage device
choices.B: Capture volatile memory and current system-state information
choices.C: Power off the server and document the shutdown time
choices.D: Reinstall the operating system on replacement storage

questions.explanation: Volatile memory and live system-state data can disappear when power is removed or system activity changes, so they should be captured before persistent storage is imaged. A disk image remains important but is less volatile. Powering off the server would destroy memory-resident evidence, and reinstalling the system is a recovery action that could overwrite evidence rather than preserve it.

questions.competency: VII.A — Investigations, Logging, and Configuration Management
questions.skill: Designing reliable centralized security logging
questions.performanceIndicator: Identify controls that improve log integrity, correlation, and investigative usefulness
questions.scenarioContext: A regional financial services firm is redesigning its logging architecture after investigators were unable to correlate events across servers, network devices, and cloud workloads. Administrators on monitored systems can currently alter local logs.
questions.prompt: Which THREE measures would MOST improve the reliability and investigative value of the firm's centralized logs? Select 3 of the 5 options below.

choices.A: Synchronize event sources to trusted time services
choices.B: Forward logs promptly to a restricted centralized repository
choices.C: Allow each system owner to define an independent timestamp format
choices.D: Protect stored logs with integrity monitoring and access controls
choices.E: Disable collection of successful authentication events to reduce volume

questions.explanation: Trusted time synchronization, prompt centralized forwarding, and integrity-protected restricted storage make events easier to correlate and harder for a compromised local administrator to alter. Independent timestamp conventions impede correlation. Successful authentication records often provide essential context for account misuse and should not be categorically discarded merely to reduce volume.

questions.competency: VII.A — Investigations, Logging, and Configuration Management
questions.skill: Escalating an internal investigation that may lead to criminal proceedings
questions.performanceIndicator: Adapt investigative handling to legal and evidentiary requirements
questions.scenarioContext: An internal administrative inquiry into misuse of a privileged account uncovers evidence suggesting deliberate theft of regulated customer data. Senior management may refer the matter to law enforcement.
questions.prompt: What is the security manager's BEST next step?

choices.A: Continue informal interviews until the suspected employee admits responsibility
choices.B: Publish the evidence internally so affected departments can identify the individual
choices.C: Engage legal counsel and preserve evidence under documented forensic procedures
choices.D: Immediately delete the suspected account and all associated files

questions.explanation: Because the inquiry may become criminal and involves regulated data, legal counsel should guide escalation while investigators preserve evidence with documented, repeatable procedures and chain-of-custody records. Informal interviews could compromise the inquiry, broad publication violates need-to-know, and deleting account data risks destroying evidence. Account access may need containment, but evidence preservation must be coordinated first.

questions.competency: VII.A — Investigations, Logging, and Configuration Management
questions.skill: Detecting and correcting configuration drift through automation
questions.performanceIndicator: Apply baseline-driven configuration management without bypassing authorization
questions.scenarioContext: A manufacturing company provisions hundreds of nearly identical servers. Quarterly reviews repeatedly find unauthorized deviations from the approved secure configuration, and manual correction is slow and inconsistent.
questions.prompt: Which improvement would BEST address the recurring operational problem?

choices.A: Use version-controlled configuration templates with automated drift detection and approved remediation
choices.B: Permit administrators to maintain personal configuration scripts on each server
choices.C: Replace configuration baselines with annual vulnerability scans
choices.D: Rebuild every server whenever any configuration difference is detected

questions.explanation: Version-controlled templates establish an authoritative baseline, while automated drift detection and approved remediation provide consistent enforcement at scale. Personal scripts weaken control and traceability. Vulnerability scans do not replace configuration management, and rebuilding every server is disproportionate and may disrupt service without addressing the change-control weakness.

questions.competency: VII.B — Foundational Operations Concepts, Resource Protection, and Incident Management
questions.skill: Reducing standing privileged access
questions.performanceIndicator: Select privileged-access controls consistent with least privilege and accountability
